text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.S. tobacco giants blink: Fight-at-all-costs strategy tossed out in bid to negotiate end of smoking-related lawsuits.
- Critics tot up Pearson price: Cost of promise called C$245 million.
- Gang bill not all Quebec wanted: Conditions apply to biker arrests.
- Ottawa to move fast on Quebec motion: Amendment on school boards may come tomorrow.
- Police recommend indicting Israeli PM: Pressure builds on Netanyahu to step down as influence-peddling scandal grows.
- Leafs to propose truce with Raptors: NHL club would welcome partnership in building new Gardens, but NBA franchise is hostile.
- Precision swings Kenting deal: Drop in stock prices helps end hostile takeover battle with C$440-million friendly pact.
- Eaton's to pour C$25 million into more sales staff: Retailer says cuts had hurt service.
- Other lab's tests found plenty of gold: Bre-X official. Independent results kept under wraps, metallurgist says.
- TSE gives brokerages reprieve from fees: Says there is no link to computer woes.
- Kenting succombs to Precision's bid: Bitter battle ends as the two drilling firms seal C$444-million deal.
- TSE gives traders a free ride.
- Air Canada eyes shakeup of regional airlines.
